subject: literature
passage: At seventy-one, two years after her husband's death, Ingrid Solberg enrolled in the beginners' swimming class at the town pool. Her children assumed she was conquering a fear; the instructor assumed she wished to be safe on the ferry to the island where she spent her summers. Ingrid let them think what they liked. The truth was simpler and harder to explain. For fifty years she had been half of a pair; everything she knew how to do she had learned beside Anders or for him. Floating on her back in the shallow end, she was doing the first thing in decades that belonged to her alone, that no one had asked of her and no one would share, and she did not mind the loneliness of it at all.
stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Ingrid finds that learning to swim helps her feel closer to the husband she has lost.
choices.B: Ingrid takes up swimming as something entirely her own after a lifetime of shared experience.
choices.C: Ingrid struggles to explain to her children why she wants to learn to swim after her husband's death.
choices.D: Ingrid takes swimming lessons to overcome a fear of water that she has hidden from her family.

explanation.why: The text lists other people's explanations (fear, safety on the ferry) and then gives "the truth": for fifty years everything she did was "beside Anders or for him," and swimming is "the first thing in decades that belonged to her alone." The main idea is this claiming of something that is hers only.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not say swimming connects her to Anders; it is valued precisely because it is not shared with anyone.
explanation.B: Correct. Swimming is the first thing that "belonged to her alone" after fifty years as "half of a pair."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says she "let them think what they liked"; the difficulty of explaining is a passing detail, not the point.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Conquering a fear is what her children assume; the text says "the truth was simpler."
